questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Because of COVID, it was very important for me, that it was close and that it was a country where I knew that if anything happened in regards to COVID, that I would be okay. 
Other then that I wanted it to be somewhere cold and where the nature would be a huge aspect of my stay - which it did.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I LOVED being on exchange. It has been the best half year of my life and I would recommend it to everyone. I honestly cannot come up with on bad aspect of it that would make it a 9/10 instead of a 10/10.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy, but I'm also the type of person who just seek information right away and I normally do not wait for people to contact me. When in doubt about something just ask the universities or who ever it is that you need to get into contact with - they are there to help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Sammen organisation in Bergen are super good at guiding you and making your arrival as well as stay easy and smooth, so that was really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was VERY pleased with it, but again, that is because I seek the information when in doubt. I do know that some of my exchange did not have the same experience as me, but 9/10 times that was because they missed an email or did not seek the information themselves. Sammen is really good at letting you know what, when and how, if it is important. Example; they provided us with covid information every time there had been a press conference in Norway - that was SUPER helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I mean, Bergen doesn't really have on-campus housing. I lived at Fantoft which was the best place, if you ask me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is super easy to get to campus. Just take Bybanen like everyone else and you'll be good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in an apartment with 15 other people (which I know sounds like a lot haha). I had one roommate who I shared a nice modern bunk bed and toilet with and then we shared kitchen and lounge area with 14 others. If you are a social person and would like to live at Fantoft (which I would say is the easiest place for exchange students to get exchange friends), then I would recommend living in this kind of housing. Everything is modern and new. Besides that, you get to become a nice little family with your flatmates.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got told when and how to register and that was what I did.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a very great guide that told you how to do everything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted, and I even registered for four more courses than I should, which was great since I then could figure out what courses was interesting while being there and trying them out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stay calm, everything will be perfectly find. The people in Bergen are super helpful so don't panic.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was pretty much the same as inn Copenhagen. I just had an advantage of the courses being offered to non-social science students as well, so I luckily knew a lot of the stuff.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very much the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: SANT290-1 and SOS119

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't really have any to be honest. Maybe I would recommend, if you have the opportunity to also look at other faculties and what courses they offer. Also, it's a good idea to look at how they are placed so your courses doesn't over lap, or that you at least know if they do over lap.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It wasn't really unexpected, but I went on a lot of trips with friend and in general it didn't go on exchange with the intention to save money. Trips are great and you make a lot of great memories from them, but they are also super expensive, which is something to keep in mind

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fresh salat in general and beer are super expensive compared to Denmark. But local transport on the other hand is quite okay compared to other prices in Norway.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are SO many which are organised by the organisation Sammen.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, skiing or snowboarding in Voss, swimming in Gammel Haugen, meeting other exchange students, KODE-museums - there are SO many. And also, you don't have to go very far to see other places and a lot of beautiful nature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Please go to Lofoten
And also sign up on DNT so you go on great and cosy hiking trips different places in Norway - it is the most koselig/hygge experiences ever.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As a Dane, it is definitely easier and norwegians are very open to speaking with Danish people. If you follow Sammenbergen on Instagram, they have a lot of activities. You can also stay in contact with your group from Fadderuken if you are going in the Autumn semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness to talk to other people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Say 'yes' to as much as possible 
Enjoy the nature 
Live in the moment

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can rent free hiking and skiing equitment at BUA. Use the days you have with sunshine: there are plenty of days to stay inside (cause it's raining a lot haha), so please get out when the sun is shinning.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
My friends - I love them to death. 
And discovering my love for nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accepting FOMO and finding a good balance between studies and free time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Please go on exchange to Bergen. It is the best place, if you ask me. It doesn't matter that it's close to Denmark - it is still a very great experience. And it is only an advantage to speak a language so close to the Norwegian language.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
